# Localization status and TODO

Trayloom follows the language of **Settings > General > Language** (15 languages, the same set as Vorssaint; *System default*
follows the Windows display language). The wording comes from Vorssaint's own translation tables, so it matches the original.

## How it works

* `Trayloom.Core/Localization/Loc.cs`: `Loc.T("English text")`, `Loc.F("English {0} text", args)`, `Loc.Fmt(value, "F1")`.
  The English text is the key. A text without an entry is shown in English.
* `Trayloom.Core/Localization/Strings.<locale>.json`: one embedded table per language, generated by `scripts/l10n` (see its README).
* The language changes live, like in Vorssaint: Settings is recreated on the same page, the panel closes and is rebuilt on its next
  opening, and tables built from translated texts (`LocValue<T>`, `FeatureCatalogEntry.Title`) refresh themselves. Windows that keep
  text in instance fields show the new language the next time they are opened. No restart prompt is needed.
* Not translated on purpose: log messages, ids, settings keys, file names, tool names reported by agents, search keywords.
* Number and date formats use the chosen language with the Windows region when such a culture exists; times use the culture's own
  short time pattern.

"Sites" counts every wrapped literal in the source; "distinct" counts different English texts. Texts that are identical in the
target language (brand names, "OK", "CPU") count as translated.

## What falls back to English, and why

1. **No Vorssaint counterpart** (about 17%, `specs/L10N_UNTRANSLATED.tsv`, one line per English text with its first location):
   Trayloom-only wording (Getting started, Tray & panel, install and first-run screens, Windows Security / winget / WhatsApp
   details, Windows Settings page names in the Command Bar, AI Agents diagnostics, many captions). Needs a translator; add
   entries to `scripts/l10n/extra.json` and rerun `build_tables.py`.
2. **Windows-adapted wording whose noun substitution is not reliable** (list below). Vorssaint's original English text exists, but the
   macOS noun (Dock, menu bar, Finder, Trash, trackpad) cannot be swapped for the Windows one in that language without breaking
   grammar (articles, noun cases, Turkish vowel harmony, Slovak declension). Substitution is done where the surrounding phrase is one
   of the known patterns (`scripts/l10n/glossary.py`); Russian, Ukrainian, Slovak and Turkish only for the phrases listed there.
   Mac -> PC, macOS -> Windows, Vorssaint -> Trayloom and Homebrew -> winget are language independent and always applied.
3. **Concatenated texts** (about 90 sites, e.g. "Waiting for approval: " + name in AI Agents, SmartAppControl.Explain,
   install window paragraphs): the pieces are not whole sentences, so they are left in English and should be rewritten as
   `Loc.F` templates before translating.
4. **Mac-only wording with no Windows counterpart** is not shipped at all (see `specs/REA_AUDIT.md`).
5. Texts whose Windows English differs semantically from Vorssaint's (Ctrl/Alt instead of Command/Option, "Task View" instead of
   "Mission Control", "Snap" instead of "tiling", ...) were matched only when identical, so they fall into group 1.
